description: A long-tailed blackbird with glossy iridescent plumage and pale yellow eyes, often strutting across lawns.
A slender buff-and-gray ground songbird that bobs its tail while walking on open fields and shorelines.
A slate-gray sparrow with a pale pink bill and white outer tail feathers, common at winter feeders.
A tiny wood songbird with a bluish-gray back, a golden throat, a green back patch and white wingbars.
A powerful raptor with a dark hood that dives at tremendous speed to strike other birds in flight.
A slender gray-brown bird with a long pointed tail that gives a soft, sorrowful cooing call.
A small olive songbird of marshes and wet thickets; the male wears a black mask above a golden bib.
A small songbird of mixed forests with a slate-gray head, bold white spectacles and yellowish flanks.
A large sparrow with a black hood, rufous sides and white belly that scratches noisily in leaf litter.
A huge raptor with a dark brown body, a snowy head and tail, and a massive hooked beak.
A small seed-eating songbird; breeding males are bright lemon with black wings and cap, feeding on thistle.
A crow-sized accipiter with short rounded wings and a long rounded tail that hunts songbirds in woodlands.
A large brown bird with a black bib, spotted belly and pale rump, often feeding on ants on the ground.
A small gray songbird with a pointed tuft, large dark eyes and rusty flanks, frequent at feeders.
A sleek brown songbird with a crest, black mask and yellow-tipped tail that travels in flocks eating berries.
A stocky songbird of southern forests; the adult male is entirely rose-colored and it eats bees and wasps.
A small seed-eating songbird; the male has a blue head, green back and scarlet underparts.
A meadow songbird; the breeding male is black below with a buffy nape and white back, singing a bubbling song.
A small olive songbird of dense thickets with yellow spectacles, pale irises and an emphatic, scolding song.
A glossy black marsh songbird whose male shows bright scarlet shoulder patches edged in yellow.
A square-tailed aerial songbird with a pale forehead and buffy rump that builds gourd-shaped mud nests under bridges.
A secretive grassland songbird with an olive head, flat crown and a short hiccuping song.
An elegant black-and-white raptor with a deeply forked tail that glides over southern swamps catching insects.
A small finch-like songbird; the breeding male is entirely deep blue and sings from roadside wires.
A small plump quail of brushy fields with a bold face pattern and a whistled call of its own name.
A large brown-and-white raptor that plunges feet-first into water to catch its prey.
A tiny slender songbird, bluish above with a long black-and-white tail it constantly flicks.
A small striped songbird that clambers along trunks and branches like a nuthatch, probing bark for insects.
A small, fierce falcon with a streaked chest that chases down small birds in fast, direct flight.
A dark olive-gray songbird of coastal salt marshes with a yellow spot in front of the eye.
A streaky brown open-country songbird with white outer tail feathers and a chestnut shoulder patch.
An aerial songbird with iridescent blue-green upperparts and clean pale underparts that nests in cavities and boxes.
A small blackbird that lays its eggs in other songbirds' nests; the male has a glossy black body.
A streaked grassland songbird with a short notched tail and a yellowish stripe above the eye.
A long-tailed rufous songbird with a heavily streaked breast that mimics other species' songs, repeating phrases twice.
A plain gray-olive songbird of tall deciduous trees along rivers, singing a long, rambling, liquid song.
A plain gray-brown tyrant that wags its tail and often nests under bridges and eaves.
A small songbird with a golden breast streaked dark, a gray cap and a tail crossed by a white band.
A small bright lemon-colored songbird; the male wears a neat dark cap, flitting through low willow thickets.
A small flat-headed songbird of open prairies whose thin buzzy song resembles an insect.
A bird of northern burned conifer forests with a solid dark back that flakes bark off dead trees.
A small colorful falcon with rufous back and two black facial stripes that hovers over fields.
A ground-walking songbird with an orange stripe atop its head that builds a domed nest on the forest floor.
A little olive empidonax of shady streamside forests that gives an explosive two-note call.
A brownish ground-feeding songbird with a rusty cap and golden undertail that constantly bobs its tail.
A secretive coastal songbird with an orange face triangle, nesting in tidal wetland grasses.
A large dark scavenger with a bare red head that soars with wings held in a shallow V.
A swamp-dwelling icterid with pale yellow eyes whose fall plumage is edged with rufous.
A cigar-shaped aerial insectivore with long narrow wings that twitters overhead and roosts in masonry towers.
A crested songbird with a thick red bill; the male is entirely bright red with a black face.
A tiny gray songbird with a black cap and bib and white cheeks, common in southeastern woods.
A long-legged raptor with a black cap, bare orange face and white neck that often walks on the ground.
A shy songbird of open southern pine woods with a sweet, varied song and plain buffy breast.
A large Arctic-breeding buteo with feathered legs and a dark wrist patch that hovers over winter fields.
A pale ashy tyrant with a large dark bill and dark mask, found on Caribbean and Florida coasts.
A tiny streaked songbird of wet grassy meadows with a short cocked tail and a dry chattering song.
A tame, dark gamebird of boreal conifer forests; the male has a red comb above the eye.
A small streaky brown songbird with yellow wing flashes and a sharply pointed bill.
A tiny olive songbird of conifers with a striped face and a bright yellow-orange patch atop its head.
A barred gamebird of tallgrass grassland whose males inflate orange neck sacs while booming on leks.
A bird that drills neat rows of holes in tree bark and returns to drink the flowing sap.
A tundra gamebird that turns pure white in winter and has feathered feet for walking on snow.
A gray predatory songbird with a black mask and hooked bill that impales prey on thorns.
A shy songbird with finely streaked buffy breast and gray face that skulks in wet thickets.
A small songbird of northern spruce forests with a brown cap and rusty flanks.
A tiny olive songbird with a bold white eye ring that constantly flicks its wings.
A stocky songbird whose bill tips overlap, used to pry seeds from conifer cones; males are brick-colored.
A large chicken-like wading bird with a rusty breast and barred flanks, found in inland reedbeds.
A grayish, chicken-like bird of coastal tidal wetlands known for its loud clattering calls at dusk.
A crested waterfowl of forested swamps that nests in tree cavities; the male has an iridescent multicolored head.
A tropical seabird with a chocolate-colored head and back, pale belly and yellowish feet that plunge-dives.
A medium-sized seabird with yellow legs and a dark band near the bill tip, frequent in parking lots.
A small shorebird that spins in circles on open water to stir up food.
A large white wading bird with a bare gray head and heavy down-curved bill, feeding by touch in shallow water.
A slender dark wading bird with a white belly and long thin neck that hunts in coastal marshes.
A black-and-white seabird that nests densely on sea cliff ledges and dives deep for fish.
A large black-and-white shorebird with a long bright orange bill used to pry open shellfish.
A small oceanic seabird with solid dark wingtips that nests on narrow cliff ledges.
A large brown shorebird with a striped crown and a long down-curved bill.
A small white wading bird with a slender black bill, black legs and bright yellow feet.
A stocky long-billed shorebird of wet meadows that makes a winnowing sound in display flights.
A small brown diving waterbird with a thick chicken-like beak, frequent on ponds.
A dark seabird with a large orange bill and long golden head plumes in the breeding season.
A small dark seabird with a notched tail and white rump that visits nesting burrows only at night.
A huge black seabird with long angular wings and deeply forked tail that steals food from other seabirds.
A dark gull-like seabird with pointed central tail feathers that chases terns to steal their fish.
A large gray shorebird that flashes a bold black-and-white wing pattern in flight.
A dark tropical seabird with a pale forehead that nests on islands like the Dry Tortugas.
A sea waterfowl of Arctic waters; the male has an orange frontal shield and a pale blue crown.
A small waterfowl with a black neck, pale chin strap and stubby bill, breeding on Arctic tundra.
A small long-winged shorebird that shows a pale patch above the tail in flight.
A pale seabird with whitish wingtips that winters along the northern Atlantic coasts.
A large ocean seabird with a dark cap and white collar that glides low over waves of the Atlantic.
A small Arctic seabird with a notched tail and a striking triangular wing pattern.
A slender shorebird with bright golden limbs and a thin straight bill, often in flocks on mudflats.
A small shorebird with a slightly drooping bill; breeding adults have a rufous back and black belly.
A seabird of the North Pacific with a big yellow-and-red bill and a fleshy spike above each eye.
A small black-and-white seabird of warm Atlantic waters that flutters low over the sea.
A dark brown dabbling waterfowl with a pale head and violet wing patch, found in eastern marshes.
A long-necked grassland shorebird with small head and large eyes that perches on fence posts.
A large diving waterbird with a checkered back and black head, known for its haunting wailing calls.
A tall shorebird with bright golden limbs and a long slightly upturned bill that gives loud ringing calls.
A plump shorebird that turns robin-colored below in breeding season and feeds on horseshoe crab eggs.
A long-necked waterbird that spears fish underwater and dries its spread wings while perched.
A dark sea waterfowl; the male has white head patches and a large multicolored bill.
A tiny seabird with a yellow bill and white forehead that nests in colonies on sandy beaches.
A tiny brown shorebird with yellowish legs that feeds on muddy edges of marshes.
A slender pied shorebird with extremely tall pink legs and a needle-like bill.
A chunky shorebird with a very long straight bill that feeds with a rapid sewing-machine motion.
A tall shorebird with a slightly drooping bill that feeds belly-deep in shallow ponds.
A sparrow-sized, secretive marsh bird with a dark gray body and white-speckled back.
A very large nocturnal raptor of boreal forests with a huge round facial disk and small yellow eyes.
A pale raptor with dark shoulder patches that hovers over grasslands hunting rodents.
A small songbird with a dark cap, white cheeks and rich rufous back, living in Pacific forests.
A tiny songbird with a dark cap and bib and white cheeks, common at feeders in the north.
A tiny gray songbird with a long tail that travels in chattering flocks and builds a hanging sock-like nest.
A songbird of mountain conifer forests; the male has a yellow body, black wings and a red face.
A slim raptor with a white rump and owl-like face that glides low over wetlands and fields.
A long-tailed pied corvid with iridescent wings, frequent in open ranch country.
A pale tyrant of open arid country with a rusty belly and dark tail.
A pale gray tyrant with salmon-pink flanks and an extremely long forked tail.
A gray-headed tyrant with a yellow belly and dark tail with white edges, perching on fences.
A large gamebird of mountain forests; males inflate purplish neck sacs during display.
A crestless blue-and-gray corvid of oak woodlands and suburbs along the Pacific coast.
A gray corvid of high mountains that caches thousands of pine seeds each autumn.
A sleek grayish crested songbird with rusty undertail feathers that wanders in winter flocks.
An Arctic gamebird with feathered feet that turns white in winter and lives on barren stony slopes.
A small streaked songbird of arid western shrublands with yellow eyes and a long, warbling song.
A chunky gray songbird that bobs on rocks and walks along the bottom of fast mountain streams.
A large gamebird of arid western shrublands whose males display with spiky tails and inflated chest sacs.
A tiny orange-brown nectar feeder that migrates long distances and aggressively defends flowers.
A sparrow-like songbird of grasslands with a yellow breast and dark bib, singing its own name.
A colonial icterid of California marshes whose male has red shoulder patches bordered by white.
A marsh icterid; the male has a dark body with a bright golden hood and white wing patches.
A large songbird with a bold chestnut-and-white head pattern and a dark central breast spot.
A stocky grassland songbird; breeding males are black with large white wing patches.
A dark brown raptor with chestnut shoulders that hunts cooperatively in family groups in the desert.
A thrush of open western country; the male is entirely sky-colored and hovers while hunting insects.
A small prairie songbird; the breeding male has a black belly and a rufous nape.
A large songbird of western thickets with a yellow patch on its head bordered in dark stripes.
A large sparrow with a black hood, rufous sides and white spots on its dark back.
A very large pale seabird with entirely white wingtips that breeds in the Arctic.
A small seed-eating songbird; the male has a turquoise head, orange breast and white wingbars.
A small seed-eating songbird with a bright yellow belly and dark back, frequent in western gardens.
A tundra-breeding songbird whose male has an orange-tan body and black-and-white face.
A tiny plump seabird with a stubby red bill that nests in huge colonies in Alaskan talus slopes.
A small dark seabird with a curly forehead plume, orange bill and citrus scent.
A gray-brown seabird with a pale knob on its bill and white facial plumes during breeding.
A sea waterfowl; the male is entirely dark with a bright yellow-orange knob on its bill.
A pale seabird with a thick dark bill that catches insects and crabs over wetlands and fields.
A large white waterfowl with a black bill, often showing a small yellow spot before the eye.
A plump gamebird with a forward-drooping teardrop-shaped plume and a scaled belly.
A tiny songbird of ponderosa pine forests that travels in noisy flocks and roosts communally.
A bird of Pacific coast forests with a bright crimson head and chest that drills sap wells.
The smallest North American gamebird of its family, living on alpine tundra and turning snowy in winter.
A brown songbird with pinkish wash on its belly and wings, living on high alpine snowfields.
A medium-sized nectar feeder of the Pacific coast; males have an iridescent rose-pink crown and throat.
A massive scavenger with a bare head and a wingspan near three meters, critically endangered.
An all-dark shorebird with a bright red bill and pale pink legs, found on rocky Pacific shores.
A stocky gray shorebird that feeds on rocky coastlines where waves crash.
A small sea waterfowl; males have a white head with green tufts and a chestnut breast.
A small seabird that nests on mossy branches high in old-growth coastal forests.
A tiny long-tailed raptor active by day, with false eye spots on the back of its head.
A plain gray tyrant of mountain woodlands that sallies from dead branches for insects.
A dark tyrant with a white belly that perches near water and wags its tail.
